chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ubaydah al-Naysaburi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Harun ibn Ishaq (meaning al-Hamdani) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Ziyad ibn 'Ilqa and 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said:

I was with my father near the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and I heard him say: 'After me, there will be twelve leaders.' Then he lowered his voice. I asked my father: 'What did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say when he lowered his voice?' He said: 'He said: They are all from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number and lineage of his successors?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Khisal establishes the foundational Shia doctrine of the Twelve Imams, emphasizing their Qurayshi lineage as a prerequisite for legitimate succession (Imamah). The Prophet's whispering of the phrase 'all of them from Quraysh' underscores the continuity of leadership within the Prophet's own tribe, a key criterion distinguishing the Ahl al-Bayt's claim from other caliphates. This hadith serves as a primary textual proof (hujjah) for the specific number and tribal origin of the Infallible Imams in Shia theology.
